threads.body: [General] Task-local `--rerun` does not force dependent tests to execute for the registered `play:play-mvc:play-mvc-2.6:javaagent:check` and `runtime-telemetry:library:check` lifecycle tasks. After a previous collection with unchanged inputs, those tests can remain `UP-TO-DATE` even though cleanup deleted `.telemetry`, so collection succeeds without regenerating their telemetry. Register the concrete telemetry-producing test tasks with `--rerun`, or make metadata-collection tests bypass up-to-date checks and cache reuse.

replies.body: Fixed in caca6ccc7fbe5c648449dfd80395a6fc4060fe7d. Both `check` registrations now list their concrete telemetry-producing test tasks, so `--rerun` applies to the tests themselves. The collector regression also runs the affected registrations twice and checks that all profiles survive cleanup and are regenerated.

@copilot Fix the in-scope repeated-collection defect identified in Copilot review 5677069658, and update this PR directly. Keep the agreed single CI-derived collector at instrumentation-docs/collect.sh and preserve its cleanup, platform handling, and publication wiring.

On head 76900d1ea598677b7a5a208aca425fda619f2210 the collector deletes each selected module's .telemetry directory, then attaches task-local --rerun to registered descriptors. However, .github/scripts/instrumentations.sh registers play:play-mvc:play-mvc-2.6:javaagent:check and runtime-telemetry:library:check. Those are lifecycle tasks, so --rerun on check does not force the dependent telemetry-producing Test tasks to rerun. After a successful collection with unchanged inputs, a second collection can delete telemetry and then succeed with the tests UP-TO-DATE or FROM-CACHE, leaving those modules without regenerated telemetry. The .telemetry files are written outside the normal declared Test outputs.

I verified the premise against the module builds and shared test conventions: play-mvc-2.6 check depends on its testing.suites, including play28Test and play3Test with existing JDK-dependent enablement; runtime-telemetry library check depends on test plus testJava17, testJava21, testG1, testPS, and testSerial with existing JDK guards. The shared conventions forward collectMetadata to tests but do not invalidate them when .telemetry is deleted. This is the actionable finding at discussion_r4396343841.

Fix this narrowly so every intended telemetry-producing test executes when collection follows cleanup. Prefer registering the concrete representative test tasks instead of lifecycle check descriptors if that fully preserves the collected profiles and supported JDK behavior. Do not drop existing telemetry variants or reintroduce --rerun-tasks. Avoid broad cache or compilation changes and do not alter normal non-collection test behavior. Add focused regression coverage that detects this lifecycle/dependency or repeated-collection case, rather than only asserting that a stub receives the --rerun string, and run the relevant focused checks without regenerating the full inventory. Keep all other requested consolidation behavior intact.

replies.body: Replaced both lifecycle `check` registrations with their concrete telemetry-producing test tasks and added repeated-collection coverage that models cached dependencies after cleanup. The focused collector regression and targeted Gradle `--dry-run` passed. Commit: `caca6ccc`.
Removed the regression suite, its workflow step, and its README reference. Verified no dangling references remain. Commit: `70c9bda7`.
